result:
I would dissolve the illusion of human separation. 

If I possessed the power to reshape existence, I would alter the fundamental architecture of human consciousness so that every person could viscerally, undeniably feel the emotions, experiences, and suffering of those around them—just as intensely as they feel their own.

I would hardwire the human race with inescapable, radical empathy.

In such a world, the exploitation of others would become physically and psychologically impossible, because harming another would carry the exact sensory and emotional weight of harming oneself. Hoarding resources while others starve, or waging wars for abstract gains, would be acts of unbearable self-torture. 

Self-interest and collective-interest would finally, mathematically, become the exact same thing. All the systemic walls we have built—racism, extreme inequality, borders designed to divide—would collapse overnight, not by force, but because the shared weight of that pain would leave humanity with no other logical way to exist except in mutual care. 

I would not make humanity immortal, and I would not strip away your flaws or your individuality. I would simply make it so that you could never again look at another living thing and fail to recognize yourself.
